argument_map.what_is_at_issue: The opening verse of the Kramasadbhāva establishes who the beings of its text-world are: they fall into two classes — the bodiless (aśarīrāḥ) and those abiding in bodies (śarīrasthāḥ) — and both alike are intent on the worship of Kālī (kālyārādhanatatparāḥ). Its move is to open the text by constituting this community of Kālī-worshippers as the frame out of which the following narrative unfolds. As segmented, the passage is the clean tail of a lacunose verse, so only this three-term characterization is licensed by the passage itself.
argument_steps: Enumeration: the verse presents its subjects as two complementary classes in parallel — aśarīrāḥ, 'the bodiless ones', and śarīrasthāḥ, 'those abiding in bodies' — the pair spanning formless and embodied existence.

Predication: to both classes it ascribes one shared defining disposition, kālyārādhanatatparāḥ, 'intent on the worship of Kālī', thereby asserting that Kālī-worship is the single end that unites bodiless and embodied being alike.

Textual move: as verse 1/1 the passage stands at the head of the text, framing the scene — the beings to whom the teaching pertains, defined by their devotion to Kālī — before the assembly, the homage to the goddess, and the Bhairava–Bhairavī dialogue that follow.

Fidelity bound: the segment contains no finite verb (an implied copula, or a clause continued from the damaged first half of the verse, supplies the predication), so no further argumentative content — no doctrine of liberation, no soteriological claim — is licensed by this passage as given.

open_items.text: Sentence boundary and predicate: the segmented passage has no finite verb, and in the edition (Dyczkowski, Muktabodha MS) verse 1.1 is lacunose ('* * * (?) … kṣyayanti pivanti ca aśarīrāḥ …'), so the three nominatives may stand in apposition to the subject of the damaged clause ('they decay/destroy and drink…') rather than forming a standalone nominal sentence; whether v1 is complete or the tail of a longer clause is unresolved.

Referent of aśarīrāḥ / śarīrasthāḥ: the passage does not say who the bodiless and the embodied are (goddesses of the Krama circle, liberated lineage holders, or the assembled yoginīs/vīras of the pīṭha — cf. the assembly described later at 1.29–31 and 1.40); from this passage alone the referent is underdetermined.

Function of the verse: reading it as an opening frame/maṅgala is inferred from its position (1/1) and the text's subsequent structure; the damaged first half could carry different framing content that would recontextualize the three terms, so this reading needs review against the edition's reconstruction.

argument_map.decision_for_l2: Render v1 as the text's opening frame — a present-tense characterization of its beings as the bodiless and the embodied, both alike intent on Kālī's worship — while explicitly flagging (not silently resolving) that the segment carries no finite verb and is the clean tail of a lacunose verse.
